newsitem.title: DENMARK: Gunmen wound one in latest Danish biker raid.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen wound one in latest Danish biker raid.

text.p: Gunmen attacked a Hell's Angels clubhouse in the Danish town of Roskilde on Sunday, wounding an occupant in the leg and shoulder in the latest episode of a Nordic biker war, state-run Radio Denmark said.

At least two men armed with a light machinegun and a semi-automatic rifle raked the motorcycle gang's clubhouse with fire while the gates were open to admit a car. The injured man's life was not in danger, it said.
It was the second attack in 10 days on the building, in a small seaside town, 30 km (20 miles) southwest of Copenhagen.
On September 12 a car bomb demolished an outhouse at the site and hurled wreckage up to 150 metres (yards) across the densely-populated residential area but caused no injury.
A turf war between the Hell's Angels and the rival Bandidos -- both Nordic offshoots of U.S. motorcycle clans -- flared in 1994 when a Hell's Angel member was murdered in Helsingborg in Sweden.
The most recent killing was in July when a Danish Bandido was shot dead near the city of Drammen in Norway.

In Denmark, a series of attacks on biker premises in built-up areas has led to growing pressure by residents to force the gangs out of town centres to areas where there is less danger of bystanders being caught in the crossfire.
Copenhagen city council on Friday ordered Hell's Angels to quit immediately their inner city stronghold after they refused offers of alternative sites.
